we present an approach to accurately track the geometry of deforming objects from point clouds acquired from a single viewpoint.

we present a robust method for the tracking of deforming objects that is applicable to noisy point clouds and that we present a method to reconstruct the complete geometry of an object by combining the use of a template with the use of a finite element method.
we present a method to robustly track deforming objects from noisy point clouds captured from one viewpoint, and that we demonstrate its applicability on real data.

a new approach to the problem of reconstructing deforming surfaces from a single viewpoint.
the development and evaluation of a method for the tracking of deforming objects from a single camera.
the problem of recovering the geometry and the motion of a deformable surface, given a set of point clouds of the object at different time instances.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method presented in this paper is a robust approach for tracking deforming objects from point clouds.

we present a novel approach for tracking deforming objects that is based on the use of finite element methods and that is able to track objects with complex shapes, even if the point clouds used for the tracking have a low quality.
the method can track deformations that are too fast and large for standard tracking methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of prior information and a finite element based approach can provide robust tracking results for objects that undergo large deformations, even when only partial information is given.

the combination of a linear finite elements method for predicting the deformation of an object with a template-based tracking method allows the accurate reconstruction and tracking of the observed as well as unobserved sides, even for noisy point clouds.
the use of a finite element based model of the object allows the accurate reconstruction even of parts of the object that are not observed.
